summary:
Rio Grande do Norte recorded zero trans killings in 2024 but jumped to 4 in 2025—the sharpest deterioration in the ANTRA dataset. Against a population of ~3.5 million, four cases yields approximately 1.14 killings per million per year, the highest per-capita rate among all 27 units in 2025 and roughly three times the national figure of ~0.38/million. The dossier cautions against reading a single-year zero as safety and notes the volatility.

This rate-driven exposure puts RN about 0.11 below the national 0.71. Compared with Ceará (0.61), RN's absolute count is lower (4 vs 8) but the per-capita risk is actually higher; the deviation from national is therefore slightly larger than one might expect from the raw numbers. The state sits within the Northeast bloc that accounted for 38 of 80 national killings in 2025.

No state-level statutory restriction or unique legal finding applies; the risk is purely a violence-rate signal. For a visitor, the small absolute numbers mean a single incident dramatically shifts perception, and the volatility suggests the environment can turn rapidly.

sources.summary: Sergipe em Debate report (27 Jan 2025) on the ANTRA dossier for 2024: 122 trans and travesti killings (16% down from 145 in 2023, close to the 125/year 2008-2024 average), five of them human-rights defenders, 95.9% of victims travestis/trans women, and systematic under-counting because official bodies do not record LGBTQIA+ victims properly — the dossier basis for Rio Grande do Norte appearing with zero recorded killings in 2024 before jumping to 4 in 2025.

SBT News report on the 9th ANTRA dossier (2025 data): Brazil 80 killings, 18th straight year topping the global tally; the state ranking places Ceará and Minas Gerais top with 8 each, while Paraíba and Rio Grande do Norte appear with 4 each — RN's jump from zero in 2024 makes it the sharpest deterioration in the dataset; the Northeast recorded 38 of the 80 killings.
